extracted.intended_audience: general readers interested in mathematics, mathematics educators, students, and mathematicians
extracted.subtask_description: A blog review/essay about Francis Su's book Mathematics for Human Flourishing that articulates criteria for what makes mathematics valuable to humans and how math education and practice should be shaped to promote human flourishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extrinsic value of mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: on math’s usefulness in real-world applications like internet searches, GPS technology, compression and recovery of images, encryption, the handling of large data, and the like.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as the pragmatic reason many non-mathematicians (e.g., relatives, many students) think math is worth learning — an argument about utility and applied impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intrinsic value of mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: on math’s beauty, universality, timelessness, ability to amaze and inspire awe, its endless depth and richness, and its ability to spark joy and fun.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framed as the inward reasons mathematicians (and some students) pursue and teach mathematics — aesthetic and intellectual fulfillment rather than utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humanity of mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: mathematics should be open to all, but is closed off to many; whether a person is encouraged or discouraged to follow their interest in math is a human and social affair, not a mathematical one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes the point that what is considered proven and important depends on human judgment; social structures and encouragement/discouragement shape who participates in mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematics as a means to human flourishing (central thesis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Human flourishing refers to a wholeness — of being and doing, of realizing one’s potential and helping others do the same, of acting with honor and treating others with dignity, of living with integrity even in challenging circumstances. It is not the same as happiness, and it is not just a state of mind. The well-lived life is a life of human flourishing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dr. Su's central claim is that mathematics helps people flourish in these senses; the book argues mathematics communicates with many aspects of flourishing and can contribute to moral, social, and personal development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematics communicates aspects of flourishing (themes list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematics connects with themes such as exploration, play, permanence, truth, meaning, struggle, freedom, community, and love (the book expands the essay's five themes to twelve).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These chapter-topics are offered as distinct ways math can contribute to a human life; a strong presentation of mathematics should be able to engage with one or more of these themes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning in mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical ideas are metaphors; e.g., to say anything interesting about 7 you place it in conversation with other things. The meaning of words grows richer the more you use them — mathematical ideas, too, grow richer in meaning the more you play with them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implication for pedagogy: foster play and varied contexts so mathematical ideas gain nuance and richness; 'why do we settle for less in the way we learn mathematics?' is posed as a challenge to conventional instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power and responsibility in mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical knowledge and experience intertwine with power; we can use our power to uplift others by encouraging, explaining, and sharing, but we can also use it to do the opposite. Parents or teachers who transmit anxieties about mathematics may unconsciously 'use their power to close doors.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethical guidance: as one grows in mathematical power one has a responsibility to use it for good — to grow in creative power rather than coercive power, to elevate dignity in mathematical spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom through mathematical knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowledge grants freedom by revealing the options available to you (illustrated by a chess analogy: a skilled player can play well out of any position). The person unaware of their options is like a player in a bad position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Educational implication: math education should promote freedom by cultivating understanding; learners must strive for deep understanding even when their formal education does not prioritize it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement and inclusivity as evaluative criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Believe that you and every person in your life can flourish in mathematics; every person is capable of greater depth and richness than commonly credited (illustrated by Christopher Jackson's story).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: judging potential or closing doors; positive practice: encourage, open access, and avoid transmitting fear or bias that discourages pursuit of mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of narrative and personal stories in mathematical pedagogy
rubrics_metrics.description: Dr. Su weaves together events from his own life, stories from his students and historical figures, and letters (notably Christopher Jackson's) to demonstrate mathematics' human impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guideline for communicating mathematics: incorporate human stories and real experiences to show transformative power and to make abstract ideas relatable and morally resonant.
